title: Chapter 214: A Seven-Week Miracle
html:
“Intermediate difficulty? No problem,” Chen Ge agreed readily. He would begin with Mu Yang High School. If they survived, he could invite them into the Third Sick Hall.

“Then I thank you in advance.” After hanging up, the owner marveled at Chen Ge’s friendliness.

Their visit delighted Chen Ge. Since the Third Sick Hall opened, no visitors had qualified to challenge it, and being unable to share such a treasure pained him. Tian Teng’s employees spent their lives inside a Haunted House; surely they possessed more courage than ordinary visitors.

“The mannequins should have set by now. I’ll use them to decorate the Third Sick Hall tonight.” He intended to adapt what he had learned from Tian Teng Medical School, then test the improvements on Tian Teng’s own staff. At lunch, he carried his proposal to the administration building. “Director Luo, I’d like you to review something.”

Director Luo sat before his laptop, brow deeply furrowed. His expression eased slightly when Chen Ge entered. “If you need anything, ask Uncle Xu. I told him to give you his full cooperation.”

“This is beyond his authority.” Chen Ge placed the document he had spent all night preparing on the desk. “I want to build a multipurpose facility beside the Haunted House. My long-term plans require something substantial.”

Director Luo read the proposal twice, then set it down. “The park is in financial trouble. Keeping it open is already difficult. We have no budget for new attractions.”

“This building would pay for itself. A café would give visitors somewhere to recover, while limited-edition souvenirs commemorating completed scenarios would encourage them to attempt more.”

“I know you’re confident, and I believe in your ability, but we must consider the larger picture.” Director Luo turned the laptop toward him. “This is a promotional video for eastern Jiujiang’s futuristic theme park. Watch it before you say anything more.”

Director Luo pressed play. A massive whale breached the ocean in an explosion of spray. As it dove, the camera followed into an underwater world crowded with fish and strange marine life. Even a ghost ship cruised through the depths.

The perspective shifted to the ship’s deck. It sailed toward a deep-sea trench and narrowly escaped the eruption of an underwater volcano.

“This is one of their attractions: ‘20,000 Miles Underwater.’” Director Luo had apparently obtained the unreleased footage through private channels. “What do you think?”

Chen Ge now understood Director Luo’s grim expression. The video alone inspired awe; experiencing the attraction in person would be exhilarating.

“The competition is formidable, but we still have a chance.” Chen Ge sat on the sofa. He would not surrender until the end.

“Keep watching.” Rather than growing angry, Director Luo’s expression softened. The video shifted to a futuristic city of skyscrapers, flying cars, and service robots. Visitors explored from capsule-like vehicles.

“Their other centerpiece is Virtual City. Visitors wear 3D glasses and experience life in the future.” Director Luo closed the video. “Impressive, isn’t it? I anticipated this years ago. Third-generation parks built around physical rides would eventually be replaced by larger, fourth-generation parks centered on futuristic technology.”

“Those were promotional images. Current technology cannot reproduce everything we saw,” Chen Ge countered. “Video games often look spectacular in trailers, only for the finished product to fall short.”

“They don’t need perfect fidelity. If the real park delivers even thirty percent of that experience, curiosity alone will draw enormous crowds.” Director Luo walked to the window. “New Century Park opened at the beginning of this century. More than ten years have passed. Its prime is behind it. Starting next week, advertisements for the futuristic park will cover Jiujiang—perhaps the entire region. Our position will only worsen.”

“Director Luo, how long do we have until the park’s official opening?”

“Less than two months—seven weeks, to be precise.”

“The schedule is tight, but we can still fight. Perhaps we’ll create a miracle.” Chen Ge rose to leave, the rival park’s campaign weighing heavily on him.

“Don’t leave yet. I have something else to tell you, and you should prepare yourself.” Director Luo returned to the desk and opened a report.

Chen Ge stopped. “What is it?”

“I asked Uncle Xu to analyze last week’s visitors. Thirty-five percent came specifically for your Haunted House, and that share continues to grow.” Director Luo held nothing back. “Your attraction is now the park’s centerpiece. It reminds me of when your parents first arrived at New Century Park.”

“Everyone has been very generous to me.”

“Don’t be overly modest. You earned this.” Studying the data, Director Luo continued, “Your Haunted House now drives attendance. Many people enter the park solely to visit you, and the number would be even higher without our admission fee. They have little interest in the other attractions.”

Chen Ge listened in silence, sensing that Director Luo was approaching something important.

“We cannot compete with the futuristic park directly. Our only option is to reduce admission and attract more visitors. We planned to do so in two months, but your Haunted House’s growing popularity has moved the timetable forward,” Director Luo announced. “Park admission will fall, while your Haunted House ticket price must rise. We’re still discussing the figures. I wanted to prepare you.”
